Washington D.C. contains one tracked data center facility, CoreSite DC1, with 22,000 square feet of floor space and zero megawatts of recorded power capacity.

The absence of a megawatt figure is the most significant data point here. Floor space measures physical presence, but power draw determines how much compute a building can actually run. Without a MW value, it is not possible to say how much AI workload this facility can support or whether its power supply is a constraint.

The single facility and small footprint suggest D.C. functions as a connectivity and colocation hub rather than a site for large-scale AI training infrastructure. The major power-hungry campuses that drive AI scaling tend to cluster in states with cheaper land, abundant power, and room to expand, none of which characterize a dense urban district.

What the data does not cover: secondary facilities, government-operated infrastructure, or any planned capacity additions. One operator, one building, and one missing number leave most of the picture blank.
